annotations.title: Answer a short general question about the AI Act or the GDPR

description: Use this for a short, general question about the EU AI Act or the GDPR (AVG), such as whether a customer service chatbot has to say that it is AI or when a DPIA is required. It looks the question up in the published Praxikon answers: deterministic, no language model, and with the articles and sources. Before you call it, rewrite the question in general terms in at most 200 characters: no names of people or organisations, no contact details, no numbers that identify a person or a case. A question that looks like it contains personal data is refused. The question never goes into a URL, a server log or an analytics service. Praxikon may keep it, after a filter for personal data, to improve its answers, unless store_for_improvement is false (privacy statement, section 2.7). An unrecognised question returns no answer rather than a constructed one, and so does a question about law outside the EU: Praxikon covers only the EU AI Act and the GDPR. For one concrete system or case, the coded assessment tools give a fuller answer.

lang.description: Language of the answer. Dutch is the default.

question.description: The question in general terms, without names, contact details or identifying numbers.

store_for_improvement.description: Optional. Set to false when the user asks that Praxikon does not keep this request to improve its answers; nothing of this call is then kept beyond the anonymous daily count. See https://www.praxikon.com/nl/legal/privacy, section 2.7.

name: answer_question

answer.description: The compact answer, as the published answer endpoint returns it, without the question.

mode.description: scenario, semantic, gdpr, koppeling, out_of_scope (law outside the EU) or none.
